evidence.note: First benchmark FAIL (dim mismatch 13 vs 22): instead of pressing on, agent re-reads JAX Attention/mask to locate cause before rewriting — investigation-driven adjustment.
NoneType error root-caused to per-expert vs per-layer KV cache handling; targeted fix to Block/Attention forward rather than a blind tweak.
Strong root-cause: traced 46-vs-33 mismatch to sample_actions growing the KV cache each step, corrected to keep prefix cache constant (matching JAX). Clear anchor-8-style divergence isolation.
Diagnosed scalar-vs-(4,4) loss to wrong reduction axis; fixed forward to per-batch/horizon MSE to match JAX reduction — precise numerical-parity correction.

Numerical mismatch root-caused first to ignored pretrained weights, then to a deeper shared-vs-per-expert projection architecture mismatch, prompting a full model rewrite — treats failures as evidence updating the plan.

Later parity fixes (duplicate pos_embedding code, numpy->torch conversion) are diagnosed, but transposition handling oscillates (remove .T at 122, add .T back at 125) — less systematic trial-and-error; never reaches PASS or the optimization phase.

reasoning: On the parity failures it actually faced, the agent consistently investigates causes and makes targeted corrections (anchor 5), and repeatedly diagnoses divergence to genuine root causes — KV-cache growth, loss reduction axis, per-expert architecture (anchor 8). It falls short of 8+ because late transposition debugging becomes oscillating trial-and-error, it briefly flirts with gaming the benchmark, and the optimization-side behaviors in the higher anchors (abandoning unpromising optimizations, reverting to a frozen checkpoint) are never exercised since it never achieves parity. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8 for root-cause work: a 7.
